title: Examination of a non-pigmented skin lesion

guidelineVersions: NICE NG12, Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (15 April 2026)

brief.scenario: You are a core surgical trainee assessing a 72-year-old patient with a non-pigmented lesion on the left temple.
brief.task: Examine the lesion using a structured clinical approach and explain the most important differential diagnoses, referral urgency and further management. No clinical photograph is required; the examiner provides all findings when requested.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Identify a possible cutaneous SCC without assuming every pale lesion is a harmless BCC.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling any ulcerated pearly lesion “simple BCC” and omitting regional nodes, risk factors and the suspected-cancer pathway when SCC is possible.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Ask permission to examine and describe site, size, border, surface, ulceration and regional nodes before naming a likely diagnosis.

flow: Introduce, consent, history of evolution and risks.
Inspect and describe morphology and measure lesion.
Palpate lesion and examine regional lymph nodes.
Interpret SCC versus BCC and other alternatives with uncertainty.
State correct referral pathway and communicate next steps.

grid.label: Introduction and consent
grid.pass: Introduces as core surgical trainee; consent and privacy
grid.high: Checks pain and requests permission for nodes

grid.label: Change and symptoms
grid.pass: Asks growth, bleeding, pain and ulceration
grid.high: Adds nonhealing status and prior skin cancers

grid.label: Risk context
grid.pass: Asks outdoor exposure and immune status
grid.high: Asks prior treatment/skin cancers and history of immunosuppression

grid.label: Description and measure
grid.fail: Calls it a lump without detail
grid.pass: Describes temple site, 16 mm, border, keratin and ulceration
grid.high: Adds induration and distinguishes observed from inferred features

grid.label: Differential
grid.pass: Raises SCC, BCC and keratoacanthoma differential
grid.high: Explains fast growth and induration increase concern for invasive SCC

grid.label: Referral urgency
grid.pass: Uses suspected-cancer pathway for suspected SCC
grid.high: Explains BCC ordinarily routine unless location/size makes delay consequential

grid.label: Safe management
grid.fail: Offers to remove immediately in clinic
grid.pass: Arranges specialist assessment and tissue diagnosis pathway
grid.high: Explains tissue sampling and definitive treatment depend on skin team evaluation

grid.label: Communication
grid.pass: Explains suspicion without declaring cancer; safety net
grid.high: Checks understanding and addresses fear without false certainty

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It is probably another harmless skin spot. Let me see.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It is pink, so it cannot be anything dangerous.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The lesion is 16 mm, keratotic and ulcerated.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You have had it a while, then?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I do not need to ask about sun exposure or your immune system for a skin spot.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There is no need to feel the nodes for a skin spot.

fail.speaker: patient
fail.text: Could you cut it out today? My neighbour thinks it is only a BCC.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, I can arrange routine removal without any urgent assessment. It must be benign because it is not dark.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Benign BCC confirmed by visual inspection; no need to warn about changes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I’m the core surgical trainee. Is it all right if I look closely at your temple lesion and feel the glands around your face and neck?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: When did it appear, and has it changed in size?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: About six weeks ago, and it has become bigger.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Does it hurt, bleed or develop a scab?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: A bit tender. It sometimes bleeds and crusts.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Have you had lots of sun exposure, skin cancer before or medicines that suppress your immune system?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: I gardened outdoors for years. No previous skin cancer and no such medicines.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I inspect the site, shape, measured diameter, edge, colour and surface, and ask the examiner for findings.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Left temple, 16 mm, non-pigmented, firm raised keratotic edge, shallow central ulcer with crust.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I gently palpate the lesion for tenderness and fixation and examine preauricular and cervical lymph nodes.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Indurated edge; one small mobile preauricular node, no other definite nodes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: SCC is a concern given the enlarging indurated ulcerated lesion. BCC and keratoacanthoma are alternatives; examination alone is not diagnostic.

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Can you just cut it out today? My neighbour said it is only a BCC.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would not remove it without appropriate planning. Because SCC is possible, I will arrange assessment through the suspected-cancer referral pathway to a skin specialist. The team will determine suitable biopsy or excision and check the node.

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Does that mean it is cancer?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It may be, but we cannot know from looking alone. The urgent referral is to avoid delay in finding out and treating it if necessary.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will document the measurement and morphology, explain the pathway, and ask you to return promptly if it changes rapidly or bleeds persistently.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I’m the core surgical trainee. I can see this area may be sore. Could I examine it, then gently check the nearby glands? Please tell me if anything hurts.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Tell me how it first appeared. What is different now compared with six weeks ago?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: It started as a small spot and has grown quite quickly.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Has it broken down, crusted or bled? Is it painful?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: It crusts and bleeds from time to time; it is tender.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: What sort of sun exposure have you had? Any previous skin cancers, immunosuppressive treatment or transplant?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: A lot of outdoor gardening. No skin cancer, transplant or those medicines.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I inspect the lesion and surrounding skin in good light, measure its maximum diameter and record its exact site so a referral can be compared with later change.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: It is a 16 mm left temple lesion with a keratotic raised border and central superficial ulceration; no pigment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would assess induration, movement relative to deeper tissues and palpate relevant preauricular and cervical nodes with permission.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The edge is firm and indurated; one small mobile preauricular node; no other definite cervical lymphadenopathy.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: My leading concern is cutaneous SCC because the lesion is enlarging, hyperkeratotic and indurated. BCC remains a differential, as does keratoacanthoma, which cannot be safely declared benign from this appearance alone. I cannot infer the nature of the mobile node without further assessment.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Could you cut it out now? My neighbour says it is just a BCC.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I understand why you want it dealt with quickly. The location and growth pattern mean it is important for the specialist skin cancer service to assess the lesion and node and determine the safest diagnostic and treatment approach. I would send an appropriately detailed suspected-cancer pathway referral because SCC is suspected.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Am I definitely going to have cancer?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No one can say that from this examination. Referral means the suspicion is strong enough that we should not delay a proper assessment. The aim of the pathway is a timely diagnosis or ruling out, usually within 28 days of referral.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would document the precise findings, explain what happens next, check contact details and provide advice to contact the team if there is further rapid growth, bleeding or new lumps.

failures.move: Fails to refer a clinically suspicious SCC on a suspected cancer pathway
Commits to unplanned removal without specialist diagnostic/treatment planning for a suspicious lesion.

recovery.when: If you gave earlier reassurance about a non-pigmented lesion
recovery.line: I should correct my earlier reassurance: a non-pigmented lesion can still be malignant, and I need to assess the concerning features carefully.

recovery.when: If you confirmed BCC without appropriate assessment
recovery.line: I cannot confirm BCC without appropriate assessment. As SCC is a concern, I will organise the suspected-cancer pathway referral.

knowledge.fact: NICE NG12 1.7.4: consider suspected cancer pathway referral when a lesion raises suspicion of cutaneous SCC.
NICE NG12 1.7.5: consider routine referral for a skin lesion that raises the suspicion of BCC.
NICE NG12 1.7.6: consider suspected-cancer pathway for BCC if delay would significantly matter because of site or size.
NICE QS130: suspected SCC pathway aims at diagnosis or ruling out within 28 days of referral.
If a virtual referral is used, macroscopic and dermatoscopic images should be provided to an agreed standard and format.

recall.think: An enlarging, keratotic, indurated, ulcerated lesion on sun-exposed skin is SCC until histology excludes it.
recall.say: “SCC is my main concern, but examination alone cannot confirm it.”
do: Ask about change and risk → inspect and measure → palpate edge and fixation → preauricular, parotid and cervical nodes.

numbers.meaning: NICE suspected-cancer pathway aims for diagnosis or exclusion within 28 days; this is not a guarantee of a clinic appointment within two weeks.

recall.trap: Calling any ulcerated pearly lesion “simple BCC” and omitting regional nodes, risk factors and the suspected-cancer pathway when SCC is possible.
recall.finish: Suspected-cancer pathway referral; no unplanned excision; explain uncertainty and safety-net.

partner.opening: Examine the lesion using a structured clinical approach and explain the most important differential diagnoses, referral urgency and further management.
partner.actorBrief: Opening: “This sore patch on my temple seems to be getting bigger.” Only if asked: six weeks of growth, intermittent bleeding, some tenderness, no brown/black pigmentation, heavy sun exposure from years of gardening; no history of immune suppression; no personal skin cancer. Patient should not spontaneously tell the candidate about bleeding or outdoor exposure before being asked.

reveals.trigger: If asked about change and symptoms
reveals.finding: grew over six weeks, tender, intermittently bleeds, not pigmented.
Patient had substantial outdoor exposure; no known immunosuppression.

reveals.trigger: only after candidate states appropriate examination (lesion size, edge, ulceration, consistency)
reveals.finding: Left temple lesion 16 mm diameter, firm hyperkeratotic rim, central superficial ulcer/crust and indurated edge

reveals.trigger: only after candidate states appropriate examination (node findings)
reveals.finding: One small mobile ipsilateral preauricular node (not necessarily malignant).
